name: Gary Numan
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Gary Numan had two No. 1 singles and three No. 1 albums before he was 23, walked away from the stage at Wembley, spent fifteen years losing fans and money, and then watched [[Nine Inch Nails]], [[Fear Factory]] and [[Marilyn Manson]] line up to cover his songs.

hero.by: Numan at Glastonbury, June 2025. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: The plumber's surname and the Minimoog
eras.text: Gary Webb, a Heathrow bus driver's son who wanted to be a pilot or a pop star, spent 1977 playing punk in Tubeway Army. By the end of 1979 he'd taken a name from the Yellow Pages, a sound from a synth he found by accident, and the top of the UK charts twice.

years.cap: Tubeway Army: Numan, Jess Lidyard and Paul Gardiner, c. 1978
years.src: The Guardian: How we made · Wikipedia: Gary Numan
years.h: In Tubeway Army, Gary Webb finds a Minimoog and becomes Gary Numan
years.p: Playing punk with [[Tubeway Army|fc0bd304-cfd4-4478-9224-3446134d57fe]] and bassist [[Paul Gardiner|03e7dbb0-4d97-4a78-9b9f-bde5156a28e0]], Webb stumbles on a Minimoog during the debut album sessions and rewires the band around it. The album credits a name he took from a plumber's Yellow Pages ad.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan · The Guardian: How we made
yt: 'Are Friends Electric' on Top of the Pops, 1979
years.h: "Are 'Friends' Electric?" hits No. 1 and Replicas follows
years.p: The Tubeway Army single, written on an out-of-tune pub piano, spends four weeks at the top. Numan says it sold a million.

years.h: A John Peel session under his own name, with a new band
years.p: Numan drops the Tubeway Army name at the peak and premieres four new songs. Keyboardist [[Chris Payne|320ba2ed-9892-464a-bbfb-041019837961]] and drummer [[Cedric Sharpley|099a08a2-8d7c-4997-889f-03e7d993cb5d]] join Gardiner behind him.

years.h: The Pleasure Principle: a rock album with no guitars
years.p: Synths run through guitar effects pedals give it a phased, metallic edge. It goes to No. 1, and "Complex" reaches No. 6.
years.xp:
"Cars" reached No. 1 in the UK in September, spent two weeks at No. 1 in Canada and climbed to No. 9 in the US in 1980. Numan wrote it on a bass guitar, not his usual piano.

The sold-out Touring Principle tour that followed produced a concert video often cited as the first full-length commercial music video release.

eras.title: Superstar, pilot, retiree
eras.text: Numan's third No. 1 album came with a bigger stage show and a press that went for him with, in his words, an unnecessary level of animosity. He got his pilot's licence, bought a plane the next day, and at 23 announced he was done with touring.

years.h: The Musicians' Union says he's putting real players out of work
years.p: Critics savage the act and the MU objects to the synths. His fans, calling themselves Numanoids, don't care.
years.xp: OMD's Andy McCluskey later described the "nasty, vitriolic journalism" aimed at Numan, who was written off as pretentious and pseudo-intellectual. OMD had been his support act in 1979.

yt: 'I Die: You Die', live in London, 1980
years.h: Telekon puts guitars back and goes to No. 1
years.p: His third straight No. 1 album, after "We Are Glass" and "I Die: You Die" hit No. 5 and No. 6. Numan later filed it as the end of his "Machine" period.

years.h: Pilot's licence on the 17th, a Cessna on the 18th
years.p: Numan had started lessons at Blackbushe in 1978. The day after he qualifies he buys a Cessna 182 Skylane for £12,000, and by July 1981 he's running his own charter company, Numanair.

years.big: "Instead, I upset everybody and destroyed my career."
years.src: The Guardian: Gary Numan comeback · Wikipedia: Gary Numan
years.h: Three farewell nights at Wembley Arena
years.p: Numan in 2022, on going public with his retirement from live shows. One farewell date became three on demand; Nash the Slash supported.
years.xp:
Constant interview requests, people outside his house and then death threats left him feeling "pushed towards the edge of a cliff," he told the Guardian. "I should've just quietly stopped touring. No one would have noticed."

The retirement lasted less than two years. The box set Living Ornaments '79 and '80, released around the shows, reached No. 2.

years.h: Dance trades the machines for jazz and funk
years.p: [[Mick Karn|0cc52b63-c9bc-4130-81d3-1ca0c31804a7]] and Rob Dean of [[Japan|697e7111-5630-4c77-83f3-39821bacc61a]] and Queen's Roger Taylor guest. It reaches No. 3, and "She's Got Claws" No. 6.

years.h: Round the world in a Piper, after an arrest in India
years.p: With co-pilot Bob Thompson, Numan flies around the world on the second try. The first, in the Cessna, ended with both men arrested in India on suspicion of smuggling and spying.

eras.title: A new look every album, and the money runs out
eras.text: Each record brought a new character: gangster, Mad Max warrior, blue-haired iceman. The hits got smaller, his own label swallowed a fortune he put at £4.5 million, and by 1992 he was making records to pay off debt.

years.h: I, Assassin gets American clubs dancing
years.p: Heavy percussive funk. "We Take Mystery (To Bed)" goes top 10, and the 12-inch of "Music for Chameleons" works the US club scene. He tours America that October.

years.h: Bill Nelson walks off Warriors and takes his name with him
years.p: Be-Bop Deluxe's [[Bill Nelson|8d463dee-ffae-4028-a3af-ec8ccb595906]] fell out with Numan during the sessions and chose to go uncredited as co-producer. It's Numan's last album for Beggars Banquet.

years.h: Paul Gardiner dies at 25
years.p: Numan's bassist since the Lasers, who had struggled with heroin addiction, died of an overdose in Northolt. Numan wrote "A Child with the Ghost" for him.

years.h: Blue hair and a PPG Wave launch Numa Records
years.p: His own label's first album is his first built on computers and samplers. It stalls at No. 32; Numan blamed distribution, among other things.

yt: Sharpe & Numan, 'Change Your Mind' on Top of the Pops
years.h: Sharpe & Numan's "Change Your Mind" reaches No. 17
years.p: A one-off with Shakatak's Bill Sharpe outsells Numan's own records. Two more Sharpe & Numan singles chart later in the decade.

years.cap: Fury tour book shoot, Manchester Apollo, October 1985
years.h: White suit, red bow tie: The Fury tour hits Manchester
years.p: The Fury breaks the top 30, but for the first time none of its singles make the top 40.

years.h: Beggars remixes "Cars" and it's back at No. 16
years.p: "Cars (E Reg Model)", remixed by Zeus B. Held, rides along with the old label's Exhibition compilation. It's his last top 20 hit for nine years.

years.h: I.R.S. renames Metal Rhythm and turns the cover blue
years.p: With Numa folded, Numan signs to I.R.S. The American release becomes New Anger, remixed and recoloured, against his wishes.

years.h: Machine + Soul is made to pay off debt
years.p: Numan himself rates it a career low. After its reception he considered leaving music entirely.

eras.title: Darker, and on his own
eras.text: Encouraged by Gemma O'Neill, a fan who became his wife, Numan stopped chasing pop and made heavy, personal records, playing almost everything himself. Meanwhile the industrial bands he'd influenced were getting famous and saying so.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan · The Guardian: Gary Numan comeback
years.h: Sacrifice goes industrial, with Numan on nearly every instrument
years.p: Gemma O'Neill pushed him to strip away the recent influences; [[Depeche Mode|8538e728-ca0b-4321-b7e5-cff6565dd4c0]]'s Songs of Faith and Devotion and [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]] pointed the way. Critics liked it.

years.h: His single "Absolution" sells 3,000 copies
years.p: Numan in 2022, measuring it against the million "Are 'Friends' Electric?" sold. Fewer than his debut single as a complete unknown, he said.

years.h: A Carling beer ad puts "Cars" back in the charts
years.p: [[Marilyn Manson|5dfdca28-9ddc-4853-933c-8bc97d87beec]] had put "Down in the Park" on a 1995 B-side, and [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]]'s [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]] cut it for the 1996 X-Files album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan · The Guardian: Gary Numan comeback
years.h: Numan marries Gemma O'Neill, a fan club member from Sidcup
years.p: The tribute double album Random, with Blur's [[Damon Albarn|7d7a5fdd-0d04-4c36-8bee-906feeae239c]], the Orb and Moloko, lands just before his own Exile, and he tours the US for the first time since the early 1980s.

years.h: Basement Jaxx and Sugababes build hits on his records
years.p: "Where's Your Head At" hooks on a sample of "M.E."; Sugababes take a mash-up of "Are 'Friends' Electric?" to No. 1. Fear Factory had covered "Cars" with Numan in 1999, and NIN had redone "Metal".

years.h: After friends die in crashes, Numan stops flying
years.p: He had flown displays in a Harvard painted as a Japanese Zero. Several friends and colleagues were killed in unrelated flying accidents, and he gave it up. He launches Mortal Records the same year.
years.xp: "You'd look forward to someone turning up to have a chat with them, and they'd be dead," he said in 2009. He had held helicopter licences, instructed aerobatics and evaluated display pilots for the Civil Aviation Authority.

years.h: Thirty years on, a sold-out Replicas tour
years.p: Fifteen UK and Ireland dates, every song from the Tubeway Army album plus the B-sides, timed to his 50th birthday.

eras.title: Wembley, the long way round
eras.text: The tributes turned into invitations: Trent Reznor, Battles, Jean-Michel Jarre. Numan moved his family to California, hit No. 2 twice, and in 2022 went back to the arena he'd quit in 1981.

q: There are still people trying to work out what a genius Gary Numan is.
yt: NIN: 'Cars' with Gary Numan, London, July 15, 2009
years.h: Nine Inch Nails bring Numan on for "Metal" and "Cars"
years.p: At the O2 in London, Trent Reznor hands over the stage. Reznor later called him "vitally important and a huge inspiration".

years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan · The Guardian: Gary Numan comeback
years.h: Splinter is his first top 20 album in 30 years
years.p: Made after the family's 2012 move to Santa Monica. "Lost" started as a song about his marriage going wrong; it came out, he said, as a song about how brilliant his wife was.

years.h: Numan plays SXSW on the Splinter world tour
years.p: The tour runs on through Israel, New Zealand, Australia and Europe, and ends the year with a sold-out Hammersmith Apollo show with [[Gang of Four|d8661c02-f423-4d72-8044-40ff05daf7a1]].

yt: Android in La La Land, trailer
years.h: Moog Music gives him its Innovation Award
years.p: The same spring, Gary Numan: Android in La La Land, a documentary about the move to LA, is on the festival circuit. A year later he gets an Ivor Novello Inspiration Award.

years.cap: Numan live on the Savage tour, December 2017
years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan · The Guardian: Gary Numan comeback
years.h: Savage goes in at No. 2
years.p: His daughter, then 11, sings on "My Name Is Ruin" and appears in its video. Numan said he cried like a baby at the chart position.

years.h: His tour bus kills a pedestrian in Cleveland
years.p: The bus struck and killed an elderly man; the driver was not immediately charged. Numan cancelled that night's House of Blues show as "inappropriate".

years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan · The Guardian: Gary Numan comeback
years.h: Intruder, another No. 2
years.p: The title track arrives in January. Numan says he writes about what bothers him: global heating, and coming back as a ghost trying to reach his children.

q: I think they were even more emotional than I was.
years.h: Back at Wembley, 41 years after the farewell
years.p: A panic attack an hour before, filmed for the Sky Arts documentary Gary Numan Resurrection, and then the crowd. "I thought it might take four years," he said, "not 41."

years.cap: Numan on the Park Stage, Glastonbury, June 2025
years.h: First Glastonbury, on the Park Stage
years.p: Forty-six years after "Cars", Numan makes his Glastonbury debut.
